items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: we were listening to ... Joe Sullivan ... These were the heroes.

ctx.x: That’s right. Because Milt Fillius had given a bunch of those things. I forget that an album originally meant multiple records.

It was an album. These albums originally developed for classical music because if you wanted to have an opera, even on a twelve inch record, a twelve inch record is only going to play four and a half minutes of music on each side, nine minutes — if you’ve got an opera how many records are you going to need? So even if you excerpted them — or the © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

nine Beethoven symphonies that Toscanini did. These were in albums. They were in books with a hard cover and sleeves that, it was all together. So they began putting the jazz in these albums, these reissue programs. So we were listening, we were now ten, twelve, fourteen, sixteen years old and we were listening to the Hot Fives and we were listening to Beiderbecke, we were listening to Morton, we were listening to Oliver, we were listening to the Ben Pollock Orchestra, you know, the band with Teagarden and…
